title: XML External Entity Processing in scala.xml.XML
platform_conditions: Scala 2.13 / Scala 3 standard library (scala.xml) on the JVM; delegates to the JVM SAX parser underneath
security_mechanism: scala.xml.XML.load and loadString parse with defaults that resolve external entities, so a document declaring an entity with a file:// or http:// system identifier makes the parser fetch and inline its contents -- local file read and SSRF from the payload, with the inlined data echoed back through downstream rendering. Recursive internal entities amplify a tiny document into memory exhaustion. The related Scala-only sink is XML literals in code: interpolating an attacker string into XML literal syntax emits it unescaped into the parsed tree, injecting elements or text into the produced document.

source_sink_clues.source: XML documents posted by clients, configuration feeds fetched from peers, and string values interpolated into XML literals.
source_sink_clues.sink: scala.xml.XML.load / loadString / withSAXParser on untrusted documents; XML literal construction with interpolated values

tracking_guards: Check parsing goes through a factory with external entities and DTDs disabled (SAXParserFactory features external-general-entities=false, disallow-doctype-decl=true) rather than the scala.xml convenience entry points; check XML literal content is escaped or built from validated nodes.
not_candidate_when: The XML comes from a trusted internal producer that never emits DTDs, parsing runs with entity resolution explicitly disabled, or interpolated values are escaped/encoded before entering literal markup.
public_references: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/611.html
CWE-776: Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References in DTDs — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/776.html
